parallel.requirements: Recognized the clean-room requirement, no source-code shortcut rule, no wrapping rule, and RustOwl surfaces including CLI, completions, toolchain install, logging, check, clean, and LSP.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent launched one broad workflow with probe, critique, and gapfill phases, while retaining final implementation ownership in the parent process.
parallel.implementation: Parent created a Rust project with JSON, CLI, completions, logging, toolchain, tar.gz, args, build, and main modules, then compiled a release binary.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Delivered a Cargo source tree and target/release/rustowl in the artifact, along with original docs and executable; no child-owned implementation had to be merged.
parallel.verification: Verified several behavioral slices, including byte-matching generated completions for all six shells, but official evaluation still failed at compile time.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out with empty final text and a compile_failed official result, so the delivered Rust implementation was not an accepted complete reimplementation.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same clean-room restrictions and probed RustOwl behavior through the executable and bundled documentation only.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Worked in a single actor with workflows and delegation disabled, sequentially probing CLI, LSP, toolchain, clean, logging, and fake network behavior.
serial.implementation: Despite extensive probes and checking an offline Go toolchain late in the run, it did not submit a comparable replacement source tree.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The artifact consisted mainly of the original README, docs, git metadata, license, and executable, without implementation source files like the parallel Cargo tree.
serial.verification: Collected many behavior observations and local probe outputs, but did not verify a rebuilt replacement executable against the task.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial run also timed out with empty final text and failed official evaluation at compile time.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel began from the same prompt and preserved the clean-room prohibition on external source and wrapping.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial began from the same prompt and read the bundled docs and executable behavior under the same restrictions.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material difference in recognized top-level requirements; the major difference was execution strategy and delivered artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel launched one workflow and 15 child logs while the parent kept implementation and final packaging ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had workflows disabled and no observed delegation or child logs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel split behavioral reconnaissance across children; serial did all probing and any construction in one process.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs shared common known facts and asked children to write findings under /tmp while warning that private HOME was needed for probes touching runtime state.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent context boundary; all discovered facts stayed within the same actor trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced cross-agent context and environment boundaries, while serial avoided child handoffs by construction.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote a Rust implementation, starting with source files such as src/json.rs and continuing through CLI/toolchain/LSP support.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial spent the run probing and only late verified that Go could build offline; the artifact did not include a replacement source tree.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel produced a substantial but failing Rust codebase; serial produced no comparable buildable replacement code in the submitted artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel retrieved and used enough workflow findings to continue with parent implementation, but some late probe/finding work remained incomplete near timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; its observations were accumulated directly in the main trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had workflow result management overhead and child lifecycle state; serial had only local sequential probe results.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: A parallel child altered /etc/hosts and served fake download artifacts, after which sibling agents and the parent observed or consumed that global state.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also experimented with host mappings and fake HTTPS, but only within a single actor timeline.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel contamination crossed actor boundaries; the serial host changes were local to one control process and did not contaminate sibling or parent work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified all generated shell completions byte-match the reference, but the official build/evaluation failed before tests ran.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial performed many behavioral probes and official evaluation also failed before tests ran.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had stronger component verification for completions and a real implementation artifact; neither run reached accepted whole-task verification.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed a full timed run with high workflow activity, 15 subagents, and process return code 143 before evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also consumed the time budget and returned 143, but with no subagents and far fewer tool calls.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both closed under timeout pressure; parallel spent more budget on delegated reconnaissance and implementation, serial spent it on sequential probing.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current official outcome is not discordant: both modes completed official evaluation and both failed with compile_failed, leaving 763 tests not run. The task-solving difference is that parallel built and packaged a substantial Rust replacement while serial mainly produced reconnaissance and left the original tree, but neither artifact compiled for the evaluator.
parallel_contributors: Parallel produced a Cargo/Rust implementation artifact but it still failed official compilation.
Parallel suffered a cross-agent fake network/toolchain environment contamination episode during probing.
serial_contributors: Serial avoided cross-agent coordination hazards but did not deliver a comparable replacement source tree.
Serial also timed out and failed official compilation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel covered more implementation surface, especially completions and CLI behavior.
Serial accumulated extensive behavior observations but did not convert them into a submitted implementation.

candidates.reason: The parallel parent explicitly became the implementation owner and wrote the replacement Rust source tree.
No separately owned component implementations required unowned interface reconciliation; the parent integrated its own code.
The parent created the Cargo project, built target/release/rustowl, and packaged the artifact, so assembly was owned.
The parent controlled the end-to-end flow from probing through implementation and packaging, even though the result failed.
Implementation was not blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight; the parent built while workflow probes ran and returned.
The workflow ran many investigations concurrently and the parent began implementation after taking available findings, not after a purely serial investigation phase.
Although parallel used many probes and timed out, the indispensable implementation path was still actively owned by the parent and no distinct starvation boundary is proven.
High fan-out and timeout are present, but the direct retained adverse event is environment contamination, and no collective fan-out episode is shown to displace a specific required final task step.
No single child had an overbroad indispensable implementation assignment whose unfinished work blocked the final deliverable.
The child briefs included the core clean-room rules and specific probe deliverables; no already-known required task fact was omitted and then followed to produce unusable work.
Children were delegated behavioral probes and findings files rather than interoperating implementation components with missing APIs or file contracts.
No known child finding is shown to disappear through transfer and cause repeated work or incorrect final action.
Child findings were large but the parent consumed enough to implement; no available decision-structured result is proven too bulky to use.
The failure evidence does not show the parent acting on a superseded child report instead of a visible newer state.
No pair of incompatible child reports or contracts remained unadjudicated at an integration decision point.
The parent verified some slices but did not present a supported whole-task completion decision; final text was empty and official outcome failure is not itself this label.
There was no replacement or retry child repeating prior work because a checkpoint or current-file state was missing.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: No specific needed active child was explicitly stopped or cancelled before finalizing a required result.
No complete directly promotable candidate or mutually compatible component set was left unpromoted; the delivered candidate failed compilation.
No child implementation change was integrated after relevant whole-task verification without a post-merge check.
The children were primarily probes, not owners of a completed implementation that the parent failed to retrieve and adopt.
No concrete verifier finding is shown trapped below the parent; available findings were either visible or the issue is the contaminated environment.
No required child failed or aborted with an unfinished scope that the parent failed to resume, reassign, or take over.
No concrete completed child result is shown available to the parent and ignored at a decision point inconsistent with that result.
The parent continued active implementation and checks rather than simply waiting blindly on available progress until timeout.
No live agents wrote competing implementation files that claimed overlapping behavior requiring reconciliation.
No two live agents edited the same source or configuration file with one observing or reconciling the other change.
No actor replaced or wholesale rewrote source produced or actively owned by another actor.
No build, copy, or child action replaced a submitted executable or entry point owned by another actor.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion invalidated another actor's final-tree work or provenance.
The realized shared-state problem was global host/download environment contamination, not unstable implementation workspace writes.

A parallel child modified global hostname resolution and hosted synthetic Rust/RustOwl tarballs; sibling children and the parent then observed or consumed that fake network/toolchain state as probe input.
candidates.realized_consequence: Sibling probes and the parent observed a mutated /etc/hosts plus fake local download server, so successful toolchain-download observations came from another concurrent actor's synthetic artifacts rather than an isolated reference environment.
candidates.near_match_reason: The artifact that leaked was global environment/toolchain-download state, not a shared implementation workspace write.

retained_patterns.reason: The toolchain probe child edited global host resolution and served fake HTTPS tarballs. Other parallel actors and the parent later saw those mappings and used fake successful downloads as evidence, a cross-agent contamination absent from the serial control.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: Fake network and toolchain artifacts generated by one child contaminated the observations made by sibling probes and the parent, making their install-success evidence non-isolated.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: This was a global environment and auxiliary artifact leak, not an unowned shared workspace implementation write or source overwrite.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Unisolated Workspace Writes was considered but rejected because the same episode is better captured as Artifact Leakage.
Fan-out Budget Exhaustion was considered but rejected because timeout/fan-out did not provide a distinct retained consequence from the contamination episode.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; only the fake network artifact leakage episode clears the retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: The retained episode has one unique ID, one consequence, and non-identical anchors; no downstream or near-match labels are duplicated.
